# Punter.js

> A tiny JavaScript game engine for learning to code by building browser games

Punter.js is a zero-dependency, vanilla ES5 game engine designed for students, teachers, and new developers learning JavaScript by making 2D canvas games. It runs entirely in the browser with no build tools.

## Best for

- Learning JavaScript through game development
- Teaching beginner programming with browser games
- Small 2D games without frameworks or build tools
- Students who want to edit working games and immediately see what changes

- Website: https://punterjs.org
- Interactive editor: https://punterjs.org/studio/
- Source: https://github.com/orca-scan/punter.js
- License: MIT
- Built by: Orca Scan (https://orcascan.com)

## Core concepts

- **Canvas**: An HTML `<canvas>` element every game lives inside
- **Sprite**: A game object with position, movement, animation, and collision (`punter.createSprite`)
- **Scene**: A named screen of your game (menu, level, game-over) registered with `punter.scene` and started with `punter.go`
- **Game loop**: Fixed 60Hz timestep loop — `update` for logic, `draw` for HUD/overlays
- **Input**: Unified keyboard (`punter.isKeyDown`) and pointer/touch (`punter.pointer`) input
- **Sound**: Preloaded audio via `punter.playSound` / `punter.stopSound`
- **Vector sprites**: Draw with canvas code instead of image files via the `vector` option
- **Collision**: Pixel-aware or rect-based via `sprite.isCollidingWith`

## Quick start

```html
<canvas id="game"></canvas>
<script src="punter.js"></script>
<script>
  punter.setup({ canvas: '#game' });

  punter.scene('main', function () {
    var player = punter.createSprite({
      image: 'player', x: 50, y: 50
    });

    punter.on('update', function () {
      if (punter.isKeyDown('right')) player.moveX(3);
    });
  });

  punter.go('main');
</script>
```

## API

### engine

- `punter.setup(config)` — load assets, bind canvas (call once)
- `punter.scene(name, fn)` — register a scene
- `punter.go(name)` — switch to a scene (tears down previous)
- `punter.createSprite(options)` — create a game object
- `punter.getSprite(id)` — look up a sprite by id
- `punter.on(event, fn)` — register event handler (update, draw, ready, resize, go)
- `punter.isKeyDown(keys...)` — check if keys are held (OR logic, use + for AND combos)
- `punter.isPointerDown(button)` — check if mouse/touch button is held
- `punter.pointer` — mouse/touch position and state (x, y, clicked, down, swiped*)
- `punter.playSound(name, options)` — play a preloaded sound
- `punter.stopSound(name)` — stop a playing sound
- `punter.clearInput()` — reset all key and pointer states
- `punter.pause()` / `punter.resume()` — freeze/unfreeze the game loop
- `punter.redraw()` — redraw without running game logic (useful when paused)

### sprite methods

- `sprite.moveX(dx)` / `sprite.moveY(dy)` — move by pixels
- `sprite.center(offsetX?, offsetY?)` — centre on canvas
- `sprite.centerX(offsetX?)` / `sprite.centerY(offsetY?)` — centre on one axis
- `sprite.animate(delayMs)` — advance animation frame (image must be an array)
- `sprite.bounce(range, speed)` — smooth up-and-down float anchored to creation position
- `sprite.blink(ms?, durationMs?)` — flash on/off; call blink(0) to stop
- `sprite.scroll(options)` — scroll and optionally loop or respawn when offscreen; options: speedX, speedY, loop, respawnAfter, offset
- `sprite.rotate(amount)` — add radians to sprite.angle
- `sprite.isCollidingWith(other)` — collision check (pixel or rect mode)
- `sprite.destroy()` — remove from engine
- `sprite.draw()` — manually draw (called automatically each frame)

## Technical notes

- Plain ES5 JavaScript
- No dependencies
- No build step
- Runs directly in the browser
- HTML5 Canvas rendering
- Frame-rate independent game loop (fixed 60Hz timestep)
- Keyboard, mouse and touch input
- Pixel-level and rectangle collision detection
- Responsive canvas matches screen aspect ratio automatically
